q: Does the RBE=14.7 for SW-1573 clonogenic survival generalize to modern targeted alpha-therapy (TAT) isotopes such as Ac-225 and Th-227, which emit alpha cascades with different LET spectra (55-70 keV/um typical) than the paper's Am-241 monoenergetic 130 keV/um beam?
basis: The paper measures a single alpha-source (Am-241) at a single mean LET (130 keV/um), so its RBE value is a point estimate on the LET response curve rather than a general property of alpha radiation. Clinical alpha-emitters used in TAT (Ac-225 for prostate cancer, Th-227 for lymphoma) deliver alphas at lower LET on average, closer to the peak of the RBE-vs-LET curve near 100 keV/um.
next_steps: 1. Extract published SW-1573 or matched squamous-carcinoma cell-line survival data for Ac-225 conjugates (e.g. PSMA-617) and Th-227 conjugates from open-access clinical/preclinical papers. 2. Reweight the paper's LQ-alpha coefficient by the ratio of mean LET-integrated RBE(LET) using ICRU-40 or Katz track-structure predictions. 3. Compare predicted vs measured survival at matched dose levels. Free-endpoint: pure literature meta-analysis + LQ arithmetic, no wet lab.

q: How would the paper's phenomenological LQ fits reconcile with modern mechanistic DNA-damage-repair models (e.g. MEDRAS, TOPAS-nBio + BioDose, or the McMahon repair-misrepair-fixation framework) that predict RBE from track-structure Monte Carlo + explicit DSB repair kinetics?
basis: The paper measures gamma-H2AX foci (initial DSB induction, RBE=1) AND clonogenic survival (endpoint RBE=14.7) on the same cells. The 14.7-fold gap between DSB-induction RBE and cell-killing RBE is exactly what mechanistic repair models are designed to explain: alpha-particle DSBs are clustered/complex and mis-repair at ~10x the rate of gamma DSBs (the paper's own '~10% alpha DSBs lethal vs ~1% gamma DSBs lethal' Discussion claim).
next_steps: 1. Feed the paper's alpha-coefficient ratio (14.67 for survival, 1.0 for gamma-H2AX) into open-source MEDRAS (freely available) with the paper's LET (130 keV/um). 2. Compare MEDRAS-predicted 'complex DSB fraction' at 130 keV/um to the empirical ~10x lethal-DSB enrichment. 3. Publish the reconciliation as a note. Free-endpoint: MEDRAS runs on laptop CPU.

q: How sensitive is the recovered beta_gamma = 0.096 Gy^-2 (and thus alpha/beta = 1.57 Gy) to the assumed iso-effect level used to interpret Fig-2's 'RBE=4' for survival?
basis: This replication assumed the 10% survival convention (D10), which is standard in radiobiology. But Fig-2 caption just says 'RBE=4' without specifying the effect level. Common alternatives include 37% survival (natural LQ e-folding), 50% survival (D50), and iso-survival at 2 Gy (clinically relevant fraction size). Each choice yields a different inferred beta_gamma and hence a different alpha/beta ratio.
next_steps: 1. Recompute beta_gamma under each of the four conventions (D10, D37, D50, iso-2Gy). 2. Plot the resulting alpha/beta values against effect level. 3. Check which value best matches SW-1573 alpha/beta from independent literature (if any). 4. Report as a sensitivity table. Free-endpoint: pure arithmetic, extends existing code/pass2_extended_claims.py.

q: Does the paper's 14.7-fold survival RBE for SW-1573 (a non-small-cell lung carcinoma line) predict the RBE hierarchy observed across other lung and squamous carcinoma cell lines under alpha irradiation (A549, H460, H1299, SK-MES-1), or is SW-1573 an outlier?
basis: RBE varies across cell lines by factors of 2-3 for the same alpha source (Barendsen 1968, Belli 2000, and later reviews). SW-1573 is a specific line and its RBE need not represent lung-cancer alpha radiobiology in general. This matters for TAT dose-planning models that assume tissue-averaged RBE values.
next_steps: 1. Mine PubMed and Semantic Scholar (free API tier) for open-access clonogenic-survival papers on A549, H460, H1299, SK-MES-1 under alpha irradiation at 100-150 keV/um. 2. Extract or digitize their LQ fits; recompute RBE-at-10%-survival for each. 3. Compare the distribution of RBE-survival values to SW-1573's 14.7. Free-endpoint: literature review + LQ arithmetic.

q: Can a small ML surrogate (e.g. Gaussian Process regressor on ~20 published high-LET LQ datasets) predict SW-1573-style alpha-LQ parameters from tabulated cell-line features (p53 status, ploidy, doubling time, initial DSB yield per Gy from gamma-H2AX) with useful accuracy, allowing the paper's fit to be interpolated to unmeasured LETs without new experiments?
basis: The paper measured a single (cell line, LET) point. A GP or random-forest surrogate over the ~20-50 published high-LET LQ studies could turn the paper into a data point in a predictive model. Feature engineering is well-established: p53 status, ploidy, gamma-H2AX per Gy at low LET, and doubling time are commonly reported.
next_steps: 1. Build a curated dataset of ~30 alpha/proton/carbon LQ fits from published open-access radiobiology tables. 2. Encode cell-line features from Cellosaurus (free API) and initial-DSB yields from gamma-H2AX papers. 3. Train a GP regressor with LET as a covariate. 4. Predict SW-1573 alpha-LQ at Am-241 LET and compare to the paper's fit. Free-endpoint: scikit-learn on laptop CPU.
